title: Newsom signs order focused on AI’s workforce impacts
summary: The executive order directs state agencies to evaluate a range of approaches, including “safety net” options for displaced workers.

title: This week in 5 numbers: AI could create more jobs than it eliminates
summary: Here’s a roundup of numbers from the last week — including how many HR professionals identified training as a top priority in our 2026 Identity of HR survey.

title: When technology becomes a headache instead of a solution
summary: Ideally, HR professionals would be part of the conversation before any new technology rollout, one expert said.

title: Lawsuit pointing to understaffed HR department at Tesla cleared for jury trial
summary: The lawsuit alleges the employer allowed slurs, segregation and other racism to persist at its embattled Fremont, California, factory.

title: AI-driven change is intensifying mental health needs. Leaders may not be ready.
summary: Policies and benefits programs that extol the importance of mental health may be undermined by ill-equipped managers, Headspace’s chief people officer said.

title: The disconnect between front-line workers and leadership is growing, report says
summary: Shift-level problems are affecting well-being, and nearly three-quarters of workers have considered quitting as a result, Dayforce said.

title: How major retailers are investing in their associates to better serve customers
summary: Lowe’s is reporting success putting artificial intelligence companions in the hands of employees, while Walmart and Home Depot are betting specialized positions will better meet customers’ needs.

title: White broadcaster lawfully fired for on-air Snoop Dogg quote, racial slur, court says
summary: Termination for such conduct is lawful even when a plaintiff argues that the offensiveness is “wrongly concluded,” the court wrote.

title: Central Transport reaches $5.5M settlement with EEOC for allegedly refusing to hire women drivers
summary: The carrier allegedly selected less qualified male applicants and subjected women who applied to jobs to separate hiring procedures.

title: Buc-ee’s allegedly treated worker with a disability with ‘reckless indifference’
summary: “Inflexible thinking” can cause employers to run afoul of reasonable accommodation requirements, an acting regional attorney for the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission said.
